per_window.ps-ns: Free wt-VcPth at 298 K, pH 6.5 (700 MHz, single field): dynamic_in_window at the N-terminus and L42, F49, N58, S59, Y85, H145 (J1, r1); rest rigid on this window (J2, r1, average NOE 0.78). H24N adds fast motion at A13, M71, N72, G116, N118 (J6, r2, inference_from_mutant).
per_window.us-ms: unresolved. Single-field model-free Rex at T22, A79, G115-H117, D147, H192 (J3, r1) and missing N118 and K146 amides that return in H24N, N72D and N118D (J4, r4); no dispersion, rate or population. Mutants move the exchange to the lid hinge G139/L154 (J7, r2) or strengthen it near H24 (J8, r3). Relaxation dispersion: search_insufficient (J12; method-class queries used E. coli Pth terms).
per_window.slower_than_ms: search_insufficient (J13): no HDX, time-resolved or spin-label data in the screened list, and the method-class queries used E. coli Pth terms.
per_window.undetermined: pH-dependent N118 reappearance with two readings (J5, r5); 10 ns MD RMSF in termini, lid, base loop and alpha5-alpha6 loop (J9, r6, md_only); mutant crystal side-chain network around H24 (J10, r7, structure_only); E. coli homolog lid/helix alpha4 B-factors and tRNA-bound loop changes (J11, r8).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Unresolved: wild-type apo V. cholerae Pth at 298 K, pH 6.5 (700 MHz, single field, phosphate) has model-free exchange terms at T22, A79, G115-H117, D147 and H192 and a broadened-beyond-detection N118 and K146 amide, which the authors read as slow motion near the catalytic H24, the helix alpha3 N-cap and the lid, but no dispersion, rate or population exists and single-field Rex cannot exclude anisotropic tumbling.
open_conflicts: N118 peak recovery below pH 6 (r5): protonation of H24 altering N118 conformational exchange, or slower base-catalysed amide-solvent exchange; no CLEANEX or dispersion separates them.

Gate-lid coupling: an earlier cross-species crystal proposal held that gate opening goes with lid closing; the VcPth wild-type and mutant structures show no inverse correlation (r7). Both rest on static crystals.
questions_for_gina: The input card pairs the V. cholerae Pth sequence and NMR structure 2MJL with UniProt P0A7D1 (E. coli Pth); the fill worker set the target by sequence. Is RelaxDB VCPTH the V. cholerae data of the 2017 paper (r1)?
Should single-field model-free Rex count as us-ms detection for the WT apo answer, or stay unresolved until dispersion data exist?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Row ids are written VCPTH-rN. Card mismatch: the input sequence and PDB 2MJL are Vibrio cholerae Pth, while the card UniProt P0A7D1 is E. coli Pth; V. cholerae Pth is treated as the entry and E. coli Pth as a homolog (inference). The second read of this case was done by one model only (Claude; the Codex reader was blocked by a content filter): 7 rows ok, 1 unverified, none flagged. All VcPth NMR uses 20 mM sodium phosphate pH 6.5; Pth has a basic 5'-phosphate clamp (K107, K109, R137) that phosphate could occupy, and the wt crystal 4ZXP carries citrate in the active site; neither is controlled or shown to be an artefact. The single 2017 paper supplies every VcPth row, so nothing is independently replicated. The 2017 paper prints the lid hinge as G139/L154 in the dynamics paragraph and as G139/V153 in the section summary; J7 follows the dynamics paragraph.
